claims.text: Conventional casting or extrusion of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material yields a relatively coarse-grained microstructure.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled low-temperature annealing can recrystallize and refine the MnNiSi-based alloy microstructure without causing phase decomposition.
The proposed treatment will produce a more homogeneous grain structure.
The proposed treatment will increase grain-boundary density.
High plastic strain and grain refinement introduce a high density of grain boundaries.
The increased grain-boundary density hinders dislocation motion.
Hindering dislocation motion through grain refinement enhances strength.
Hindering dislocation motion through grain refinement enhances ductility.
Controlled annealing can prevent phase transformation or decomposition in the deformed MnNiSi-based material.
Preventing phase transformation or decomposition retains the primary magnetic phase responsible for the large magnetocaloric effect.
Compared with conventionally processed coarse-grained samples, the treated material will have higher tensile strength.
Compared with conventionally processed coarse-grained samples, the treated material will have greater ductility.
The treated material will retain a magnetic entropy change of similar magnitude to that of the conventionally processed baseline.
Annealing at excessive temperature can cause phase changes that diminish the magnetocaloric effect.
Excessive severe plastic deformation can cause phase changes or magnetic disorder that diminish the magnetocaloric effect.
